chunks: Our father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Uthman ibn Jabalah, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Three qualities: whoever possesses them, or even one of them, will be under the Shade of the Throne of God, the Mighty and Exalted, [on the Day of Resurrection], on the Day when there is no shade but His Shade: A man who gives to people from himself what they are in need of; a man who does not advance one person nor delay another until he knows that this is for God's pleasure or displeasure; and a man who does not criticize his Muslim brother with a fault until he removes that fault from himself, for indeed he does not remove a fault from himself but another fault appears to him. And sufficient is the man's occupation with himself rather than with people.

key_terms.ظِلِّ عَرْشِ اللَّهِ: Shade of the Throne of God

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that lead to being under the Shade of God's Throne on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three traits as essential for attaining the highest spiritual status under the Divine Throne, emphasizing the transition from external charity to internal self-mastery. The hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on *muhasaba* (self-accounting) and *sadr al-sadr* (forgiveness), warning that criticizing others often reveals one's own hidden flaws. This teaching aligns with the concept of *adab al-nafs* (etiquette of the soul), where purity of heart precedes purity of deed.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-3 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Mihran, on the authority of Othman ibn Jabalat, on the authority of Abi Hamzih al-Somali, on the authority of Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“There are three qualities having each of which would cause one to be under the Shade of the Honorable the Exalted God (on the Resurrection Day) on the day in which there is no shade but God’s Shade. The first characteristic is to grant to people what you expect of them. The second characteristic is to only do what pleases God, and not do what would raise God’s Wrath. The third characteristic is not to express the faults of one’s Muslim brothers in their absence, unless one first removes such faults from himself. It is better to attend to the improvement of one’s own faults than to seek out other people’s faults.”
